metadata.title: Data Density Pass 20 -- Day 3 Lee's Retreat (Ticks 580-675)
metadata.description: Individual unit records for Lee's retreat from Gettysburg July 3 afternoon through the end of the battle at tick 675. The Confederate army withdrawing to Seminary Ridge. Meade's cautious pursuit. Imboden's cavalry covering the wagon train of wounded. The end of the battle.

placements.notes: Pickett's division survivors rallying on Seminary Ridge. Pickett weeps. Lee rides among them.
Heth's division -- the men who started it all on July 1 -- holding Seminary Ridge
Anderson's division covering the withdrawal
Buford's cavalry -- Meade hesitates to pursue. The window closes.
Gibbon's II Corps holding Cemetery Ridge -- Meade will not order an advance today
Stuart's cavalry screening the Confederate right -- humiliated by Custer but still operational
Gregg's Union cavalry -- the men who stopped Stuart. Now watching Lee's withdrawal.
Imboden's cavalry brigade leading the 17-mile wagon train of Confederate wounded westward
Pickett's division beginning the retreat to Virginia. Lee's army is going home.
A.P. Hill's corps leading the Confederate withdrawal down the Chambersburg Pike
Ewell's corps beginning withdrawal -- they occupied Gettysburg for 3 days
Gamble's cavalry brigade following the Confederate rear guard cautiously
Pickett's division on Chambersburg Pike heading west -- a shattered force
Iron Brigade survivors bivouacking on Cemetery Ridge -- they held McPherson's Ridge on July 1
20th Maine still on Little Round Top -- they have not moved from where they charged 3 days ago
1st Minnesota -- 38 survivors. Three days of battle. Still in place.
26th NC on Seminary Ridge -- 140 from 843. Waiting to march home to North Carolina.
Cushing's battery being recovered from The Angle -- 4 of 6 guns destroyed. Cushing is dead.
McLaws's division on the Hagerstown Road -- Confederate army withdrawing to the Potomac
Heth's division departing Gettysburg -- they fired the first shots on July 1 looking for shoes
END OF BATTLE. 20th Maine on Little Round Top. July 3, 1863. The Union is saved.
END OF BATTLE. 38 survivors. The price the 1st Minnesota paid for one day -- and the nation paid over three.
END OF BATTLE. 26th North Carolina. 843 men entered Pennsylvania. 140 leave it.
END OF BATTLE. Armistead's brigade. Their general died beyond the wall on July 5. His hat still on his sword.
